schedule.comment: The cadence budget is each vector's scripted cycle count, so a budget and a script can never disagree.

vectors.name: rotation-precedes-poll
vectors.comment: A rotation to a successor and an update signed by that successor are both available in one cycle. Polling first refuses the update; rotating first applies it.

vectors.name: authority-behind-is-attributed
vectors.comment: The rotation endpoint is unreachable while the policy endpoint offers an update signed by the successor. The refusal is the same code as a stranger's and is attributed to the incomplete rotation.

vectors.name: foreign-authority-is-not-attributed
vectors.comment: The rotation cycle reports the host current, so an update signed by an authority the registry does not hold is a stranger rather than a lag.

vectors.name: refused-rotation-does-not-stop-the-cadence
vectors.comment: An endpoint-authentication failure on the rotation channel changes nothing, so the poll and sweep still run and the cadence completes.

vectors.name: exhausted-rotation-does-not-stop-the-cadence
vectors.comment: A rotation channel that never answers is exhausted rather than fatal, and an ordinary policy update still applies.

vectors.name: unretained-floor-stops-before-the-poll
vectors.comment: The rotation was published but its guard was not retained, so the cycle stops before contacting the policy endpoint.

vectors.name: policy-refusal-stops-with-its-own-code
vectors.comment: A poll refused for a reason unrelated to authority keeps CBI47's stop and is not attributed to rotation.

vectors.name: rotation-cancellation-precedes-any-poll
vectors.comment: Cancellation observed by the rotation cycle cancels the whole cycle with no policy contact.

vectors.name: a-later-rotation-unblocks-a-later-update
vectors.comment: The first cycle is behind and stops; a fresh cadence whose rotation succeeds applies the same update.
